## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pīṭhajātaka* (Ja 337) is a canonical birth story in the Pali *Jātaka* collection, rendered in English as *The Seat*. In the edition of the *Jātaka* and its commentary edited by V. Fausböll, it appears as the seventh story in its section, opening with the canonical verse lemma *Na te pīṭhan ti* [Fausböll 1883].

According to its opening narrative framework (*nidāna*), the Buddha told this story while staying at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthi concerning a certain monk [Fausböll 1883]. Having arrived at Jetavana from the countryside, the monk put away his bowl and robes, paid homage to the Master, and inquired of the young novices which householders in Sāvatthi were supportive and hospitable to visiting monks [Fausböll 1883].
